name: Nur Alem
view: front elevation: the 80 m glass sphere resting on its low plinth building, floor levels shown as latitude lines
note: Kazakhstan has no freedom of panorama for buildings; several Expo 2017 pavilion photos have been deleted from Commons. The only survivors are File:Storm over Astana 1.jpg / 2.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, 1920x1080), lightning shots where the sphere is not the clear subject, so drawn instead. Proportions from sources: 80 m diameter, 100 m total height, sphere set on a plinth building; plinth width is approximate.

name: Parliament Library Building
note: Only free photo is File:Parliament library.jpg (CC BY-SA 4.0, category Buildings by Raj Rewal) at 660x467, below the 1200px floor; worth using if the owner relaxes the size rule. Not drawn: sources confirm a low red-sandstone mandala plan with twelve domes of different sizes and structures (fibre cement, steel lattice, glass), but not how they line up in any elevation, so a drawing would be guesswork.

name: Paulistano Athletic Club Gymnasium
note: No photo on Commons (Category:Club Athlético Paulistano has only a 457px aerial). Sources agree on a rectangular podium, six concrete blades in a circle carrying a concrete ring, and a central metal roof hung from it by twelve steel cables, but not on the blade and cable geometry seen in elevation (whether blades rise above the ring, where the cables anchor). Too uncertain to draw.

name: Pearling Path Visitor Centre
note: No photo on Commons. Sources describe a perforated concrete roof plane on a forest of columns over the ruins of an amara, a perimeter wall and triangular wind towers, but give no heights, column count or opening shapes; an elevation would be guesswork.
